name: N-Acetylcysteine
lead: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is a modified form of the amino acid cysteine. It is an established medicine used as the antidote for acetaminophen (paracetamol) overdose and as a mucus-thinning agent, and is also sold as a supplement.

In recovery and appearance communities it is used as a glutathione precursor and antioxidant. Beyond its approved uses, evidence for skin, hair or recovery benefits is limited, though it has been studied for psychiatric and compulsive-behavior conditions.

paras: NAC supplies cysteine, the rate-limiting building block for glutathione synthesis, and can also act as a direct reducing agent and modulate glutamate signaling.

Common side effects are nausea and other gastrointestinal upset; the sulfur odor is notable. Intravenous use carries anaphylactoid reaction risk. Its US regulatory status as a supplement has been disputed because it is also an approved drug, though it remains widely available.
